dropped.item: The lesson/takeaway: 'sometimes the biggest operational wins come from meeting people where they already are'
'Closing that gap matters for both the practice and the people we serve' (the stated dual benefit to practice and patients)
Front desk teams 'spent hours' leaving voicemails (the scale of time wasted)
'when they need it': the timeliness aspect of patients getting care
'The change was simple': framing that the fix was easy
Benefit framed as 'fewer empty chairs' (the capacity/utilization angle) is reduced to 'fewer missed appointments'

changed.item: Voicemails 'rarely got returned' became 'never got returned', which overstates an absolute
Call to action strengthened from 'it's worth testing' to 'this is something that you should trial'
'If you run a multi-location practice' became 'If you have multiple practices', a slight shift in audience framing
'a patient who didn't get treated' became 'a patient that may need treatment', which hedges the claim
Closing question changed from 'What's worked for you' (asking for successes) to 'What do you do' (asking for current practice)

added.item: 'most of the time we'd have to leave a voicemail': a frequency claim not stated in the original
